```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kratochwil_2018_antiIL17_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kratochwil_2018_antiIL17_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0205435> (open access)

Kratochwil et al. labelled a human anti-IL17 IgG1 model antibody (Roche code
RO5310074, shown on the Figure 4B/C axes) with a 14C-propionate tag and
measured the plasma profile in mice by cavity ring-down spectroscopy (CRDS) and
by accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS). The pharmacokinetic data were described
by a linear two-compartment population model (Methods, "PK modeling",
Equations 5-9; Table 1). The tissue bio-distribution coefficients the paper
also reports are observed tissue-to-plasma ratios, not a model, and are not
part of this extraction.

# Population

Healthy male adult C57BL/6J mice (Charles River, France) received a single
intravenous bolus via the tail vein of 75 nmol/kg anti-IL17 containing 2.1 nCi
of 14C-labelled anti-IL17 (specific activity of the blended dose
1.24 nCi/nmol). Plasma was sampled sparsely (one sample per mouse per time;
composite profiles) at 1, 3, 7, 24, 48, 72 and 96 h, and at the terminal
necropsies at 7, 24, 168 and 336 h. The paper does not print the number of
mice. Estimation used Phoenix NLME 6.4 with FOCE-ELS.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Kratochwil_2018_antiIL17_mouse")()$population`).

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(6.69 mL/day/kg) | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (Vc) | log(49.5 mL/kg) | Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(84.3 mL/day/kg) | Table 1 |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(44.7 mL/kg) | Table 1 |
| `etalvp` | omega^2 = 0.0871 | Table 1; exponential IIV on Vp, Equation 8 |
| `propSd` | 0.153 | Table 1 'sigma proportional'; Equation 9 |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Equations 5-7 |
| `Cc <- 1000 * central / vc` (nM) | n/a | Methods: molar units via MW 150000 g/mol; Figure 4B/C axis in nM |
| Dose 75 nmol/kg IV bolus | n/a | Methods, "Pharmacokinetic study" |
| t1/2 alpha 0.190 d, t1/2 beta 9.90 d, effective t1/2 9.76 d | derived | Table 1, derived parameters (used as gates below) |
| NCA t1/2 10.4 (AMS), 10.0 (CRDS), 11.1 (gamma counting) d | n/a | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |

# Typical-value checks against Table 1

Table 1 lists three derived half-lives. They follow from the four structural
parameters in closed form, so they test the transcription directly: the two
exponents of the biexponential, and the "effective" half-life
`ln(2) * (Vc + Vp) / CL`.

```{r closed-form}
mod <- readModelDb("Kratochwil_2018_antiIL17_mouse")
p <- c(cl = 6.69, vc = 49.5, q = 84.3, vp = 44.7)
kel <- p[["cl"]] / p[["vc"]]
k12 <- p[["q"]] / p[["vc"]]
k21 <- p[["q"]] / p[["vp"]]
s <- kel + k12 + k21
disc <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * kel * k21)
alpha <- (s + disc) / 2
beta <- (s - disc) / 2
derived <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("t1/2 alpha (day)", "t1/2 beta (day)", "effective t1/2 (day)"),
  Model = c(log(2) / alpha, log(2) / beta,
            log(2) * (p[["vc"]] + p[["vp"]]) / p[["cl"]]),
  `Table 1` = c(0.190, 9.90, 9.76)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Model / `Table 1` - 1))
knitr::kable(derived, digits = c(0, 3, 3, 2))
# Table 1 prints three significant figures, so each derived value can move by
# up to about 1% from rounding of the inputs; a mis-transcribed parameter
# moves these by far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$`Difference (%)`) < 1))
```

The typical-value solve of the packaged model must reproduce the same
biexponential, and its AUC must equal Dose / CL.

```{r typical}
dose <- 75 # nmol/kg
obs_days <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.01), seq(1, 30, by = 0.1),
                          seq(30, 200, by = 1))))
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(obs_days)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ,
                           rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()

c0 <- 1000 * dose / p[["vc"]]
A <- c0 * (alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta)
B <- c0 * (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta)
closed <- A * exp(-alpha * sim_typ$time) + B * exp(-beta * sim_typ$time)
max_rel <- max(abs(sim_typ$Cc / closed - 1))
max_rel
stopifnot(max_rel < 1e-6)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

200 virtual mice, each observed at every sampling time of the study (the real
study used one sample per mouse; the population quantiles are the same). The
only random effect in the model is on Vp, plus the 15.3% proportional residual
error.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20181017)
n_mice <- 200
samp_h <- c(1, 3, 7, 24, 48, 72, 96, 168, 336)
samp_d <- samp_h / 24
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble(id = seq_len(n_mice), time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1,
         cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_mice), time = c(0, samp_d)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  mutate(treatment = "75 nmol/kg IV") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4B/C: prediction-corrected VPC

Figure 4B shows the median prediction-corrected concentration and Figure 4C
the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. With a single dose level and no covariates
the prediction correction is the identity, so the simulated quantiles are
directly comparable. The black points are the observed medians digitised by
the maintainers from Figure 4B (approximate, read off a log axis).

```{r figure-4bc}
fig4b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~Cc,
  1,     700,
  2,     700,
  3,     600,
  4,     560,
  7,     520,
  14,    280
)
vpc <- sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    q025 = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    q50 = quantile(sim, 0.5),
    q975 = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q50)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(sim_typ, time <= 15), aes(time, Cc),
            linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = fig4b, aes(time, Cc)) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(100, 4000)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Anti-IL17 concentration (nM)",
       title = "Simulated median and 95% interval, 75 nmol/kg IV",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 4B/C of Kratochwil 2018.",
                       "Dashed: typical-value solve; points: digitised",
                       "observed medians."))
```

```{r figure-4b-check}
chk <- vpc |>
  mutate(time = round(time, 4)) |>
  inner_join(fig4b, by = "time") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (q50 / Cc - 1))
knitr::kable(chk |> select(time, q50, Cc, pct_diff) |>
               rename(`Time (day)` = time, `Simulated median (nM)` = q50,
                      `Figure 4B (nM)` = Cc, `Difference (%)` = pct_diff),
             digits = 1)
# The observed medians are noisy composite-sampling points (Figure 4B wobbles
# between days 3 and 7); assert on the centre and a loose envelope.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 15,
  max(abs(chk$pct_diff)) < 30
)
```

## Figure 4A: radioactivity in plasma

Figure 4A plots the CRDS and AMS radioactivity in dpm/mL. With the blended
specific activity of 1.24 nCi/nmol and 2220 dpm per nCi, the molar prediction
converts to `Cc / 1000 * 1.24 * 2220` dpm/mL. Read off Figure 4A, the 14C
profiles fall from roughly 5000 dpm/mL in the first hours to roughly
800 dpm/mL at day 14.

```{r figure-4a}
dpm <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time <= 15) |>
  mutate(dpm_ml = Cc / 1000 * 1.24 * 2220)
ggplot(dpm, aes(time, dpm_ml)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(100, 1e4)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Radioactivity (dpm/mL)",
       caption = "Typical-value prediction; compare Figure 4A of Kratochwil 2018 (14C, CRDS and AMS).")
dpm_14 <- dpm$dpm_ml[which.min(abs(dpm$time - 14))]
dpm_14
# Figure 4A day-14 points lie between about 600 and 1000 dpm/mL.
stopifnot(dpm_14 > 600, dpm_14 < 1000)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports non-compartmental half-lives of 10.4 (AMS), 10.0 (CRDS) and
11.1 days (125I gamma counting). The simulated cohort is analysed per mouse
over the study's own sampling grid (to 14 days).

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
# The observation grid includes time 0; after an IV bolus rxSolve returns the
# post-dose concentration there, which anchors AUC0-inf.
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time, sim_nca$id, min) == 0))

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~half.life,
  "75 nmol/kg IV", 10.0
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated vs. published NCA half-life (CRDS data).",
  "* differs from reference by >20%."
))

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  pull(PPORRES)
median(hl)
# The study NCA was on composite mean profiles; the three methods gave
# 10.0-11.1 days. The simulated median must sit near that range.
stopifnot(abs(median(hl) / 10.0 - 1) < 0.2)
```

The typical-value AUC from 0 to infinity must equal Dose / CL
(75 / 6.69 nmol day/mL = `r format(round(1000 * 75 / 6.69), big.mark = ",")` nM day).

```{r auc-identity}
typ_nca <- sim_typ |>
  select(time, Cc) |>
  mutate(id = 1, treatment = "typical")
auc_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(data.frame(id = 1, treatment = "typical", time = 0,
                              amt = dose),
                   amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  pull(PPORRES)
c(pknca = auc_typ, dose_over_cl = 1000 * dose / p[["cl"]])
# Linear-up/log-down trapezoids on a 0.01-day early grid agree with Dose / CL
# to about 1e-5; a 0.1% bound keeps headroom and still fails on any CL, dose
# or unit error.
stopifnot(abs(auc_typ / (1000 * dose / p[["cl"]]) - 1) < 1e-3)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Units.** Table 1 reports body-weight-normalised parameters (mL/kg,
  mL/day/kg); the model keeps them, so doses are given in nmol/kg and the
  concentration `Cc` is in nM (nmol/mL x 1000), the unit of Figure 4B/C. To
  simulate a mouse of a given weight in absolute amounts, multiply the dose
  and the volumes by its weight; concentrations are unchanged.
- **Residual error scale.** Table 1 labels the residual parameter
  "sigma proportional" with value 0.153, and Equation 9 is
  `Cobs = Cpred * (1 + eps)`. Phoenix NLME estimates the residual standard
  deviation, so 0.153 is encoded as the proportional standard deviation
  (15.3%).
- **Equation 8 wording.** The text calls `Vp_i` "the individual central
  volume"; the symbol, the sentence before it and Table 1 all place the
  inter-subject variability on the peripheral volume, which is what the model
  uses.
- **Pooled data.** The prediction-corrected VPC is drawn for "all data" and
  the paper compares the 14C profiles with the 125I-labelled anti-IL17
  profiles of Eigenmann et al. (66 nmol/kg). The paper does not say whether
  the gamma-counting data entered the fit, but the Figure 4B/C medians have a
  vertex at day 5, a time sampled only in the 125I study (Figure 4A), which
  suggests they did. The model has no method or study covariate either way.
- **Number of mice.** Not printed in the paper; `population$n_subjects` is
  `NA`.
- **Figure values.** The Figure 4B medians and the Figure 4A radioactivity
  levels used as checks above were read by the maintainers from the published
  figure and are approximate.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article on EuropePMC as
  of 2026-11-25.
